name: Melissa Hurtado
title: California State Senator
years_of_service: 2018 to present (District 14, 2018 to 2022; District 16, 2022 to present, following 2021 redistricting)
background: Hurtado is the daughter of farmworkers and grew up in California's Central Valley. She graduated from California State University, Sacramento with a bachelor's degree in political science, becoming the first in her family to earn a college degree, and worked as a community organizer for public employees before entering elected office.

She began her political career on the Sanger City Council, winning a District 1 seat in 2016 with 68.2% of the vote. In 2018 she challenged incumbent Republican State Senator Andy Vidak for the 14th Senate District and defeated him 55.8% to 44.2%, flipping the seat to Democratic control and becoming, at the time, the youngest woman ever elected to the California State Senate.

Following 2021 redistricting, Hurtado's district was renumbered to Senate District 16. She won re-election in 2022 by 50.01% to Republican David Shepard's 49.99%, a difference of 22 votes out of more than 136,000 cast. In July 2023 she announced a campaign for California's 22nd Congressional District, finishing fourth in the March 2024 primary with about 14% of the vote and suspending that campaign; she returned to seek re-election to her Senate seat in 2026.

In July 2020 Hurtado was named to the Biden campaign's National Latino Leadership Committee, one of two California Latinas selected. She was also selected as a subcommittee co-chair of the Council of State Governments' 2021 to 22 Healthy States National Task Force. In office she has focused on Central Valley priorities including water supply and flood management, agricultural and rural health issues, and consumer protection.

voting_record_highlights: SB 557 (2025 to 2026), the Family First Act, which Hurtado authored to strengthen California's Family Resource Centers and support early-intervention efforts to prevent child abuse, was approved by the Governor and filed with the Secretary of State on August 24, 2026 as Chapter 125, Statutes of 2026.

SB 1157 (2023 to 2024), authored by Hurtado, would have expanded state contracting requirements to combat forced labor and human trafficking by requiring contractors to certify compliance and implement anti-trafficking due-diligence plans. The bill did not pass; it was held without further action in committee and died at the end of the 2023 to 2024 session (last action November 30, 2024).

SB 1219 (2021 to 2022), which Hurtado co-introduced with Senator Cortese, would have created a Blue Ribbon Commission to modernize California water law and dissolve and restructure the State Water Resources Control Board. It did not advance; both houses took no further action on it by the November 30, 2022 end of session, and it died without being sent to the Governor.

SB 556 (2025 to 2026), which Hurtado authored to fund floodplain acquisition and habitat restoration in Kern, Kings, and Tulare counties (roughly $21.5 million through the Wildlife Conservation Board), was still moving through the Legislature as of this profile's research date, last amended in the Assembly in July 2025; its final disposition was not yet determined.
attendance: The California State Senate does not publish an individual floor-attendance or participation scorecard for its members the way some city councils publish meeting-attendance logs. No such published attendance record for Senator Hurtado specifically could be located on senate.ca.gov, leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, or Ballotpedia; her voting record on specific bills can be looked up bill-by-bill on leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, but no consolidated attendance percentage is publicly available.
